RE: Appeal of Adverse Benefit Determination
Member: Rowan Carter
Member ID: W914903090
Reference Number: POC-5BA41AD17E-24277
Date of Denial Notice: 2026-08-19
Appeal Deadline: 2027-02-15
Requested Service: Partial (unicompartmental) knee replacement, CPT 27446
Treating Surgeon: Marchetti, MD, Orthopedic Surgery

Dear Appeals Reviewer,

I am writing to appeal the denial of prior authorization for CPT 27446 (partial knee replacement), denied on the stated basis that "the requested procedure does not meet the plan's criteria for medical necessity."

I understand that Aetna's applicable coverage policy for this procedure is Clinical Policy Bulletin Number 0660, "Knee Arthroplasty." That policy states, regarding unicompartmental knee arthroplasty:

"Unicompartmental knee arthroplasty using Food and Drug Administration (FDA)-approved devices is considered medically necessary for members with advanced osteoarthritis or post-traumatic arthritis of the knee affecting only a single compartment (medial, lateral or patellofemoral), and who meet the following criteria... Pain and functional disability that interferes with ADLs due to osteoarthritis or post-traumatic arthritis of the knee joint; and Limited range of motion, crepitus, or effusion or swelling of knee joint on physical examination; and Member must have intact, stable ligaments, in particular the anterior cruciate ligament; and Patient's knee arc of motion (full extension to full flexion) is not limited to 90 degrees or less; and Radiographic evidence of moderate/severe osteoarthritis (i.e., Kellgren-Lawrence Grade 3 or 4)... affecting only a single (medial, lateral or patellofemoral) compartment of the knee joint; and History of unsuccessful conservative therapy (non-surgical medical management; 12 or 24 weeks depending on age/BMI) that is clearly addressed in the medical record... with at least half of the necessary conservative therapy consisting of formal physical therapy (in-person with a licensed physical therapist as opposed to home or virtual physical therapy)."

The policy further specifies the components of conservative therapy:

"Conservative therapy includes all of the following, unless contraindicated: Anti-inflammatory medications or analgesics; and Flexibility and muscle strengthening exercises; and Activity modification; and Supervised physical therapy (activities of daily living [ADLs] diminished despite completing a plan of care); and Assistive device use (required for persons with relative contraindications to joint replacement, optional for others); and Therapeutic injections into the knee (required for persons with relative contraindications to joint replacement, optional for others)."

The submitted clinical record demonstrates that Rowan Carter meets these criteria:

1. Pain and functional disability interfering with ADLs: Mr./Ms. Carter has had 9 months of progressive knee pain unrelieved by rest, cannot climb stairs without assistance, and wakes 3–4 times nightly due to pain.

2. Limited range of motion/exam findings: Physical examination documented positive provocative testing on the affected side and range of motion limited by pain. [Specific degree measurement of knee arc of motion, if recorded in the exam note, should be confirmed by Dr. Marchetti's office, as the summary provided to me does not state the measurement in degrees; I am requesting that this be pulled from the chart and submitted with this appeal to directly address the policy's "not limited to 90 degrees or less" criterion.]

3. Ligament stability: [Documentation confirming intact, stable ligaments, including the anterior cruciate ligament, should be confirmed from the exam note and submitted with this appeal, as this detail was not included in the clinical summary I received.]

4. Radiographic evidence of single-compartment, Kellgren-Lawrence Grade 4 disease: MRI of the knee performed 2026-06-09 showed full-thickness cartilage loss in the medial compartment with bone-on-bone apposition, and was read as Kellgren-Lawrence grade 4 medially — meeting the policy's radiographic threshold and confirming single-compartment (medial) involvement.

5. History of unsuccessful conservative therapy, including formal physical therapy: Mr./Ms. Carter completed 14 weeks (2026-04-10 to 2026-07-17) of supervised, in-person physical therapy focused on quadriceps strengthening and range of motion, totaling 16 visits, as documented in the physical therapy discharge note. This satisfies the policy's requirement that "at least half of the necessary conservative therapy consist[] of formal physical therapy (in-person with a licensed physical therapist)." In addition, the record documents 8 months of NSAID use with inadequate relief and a corticosteroid injection on 2026-06-17 that produced only 2 weeks of partial relief — directly satisfying the "anti-inflammatory medications or analgesics" and "therapeutic injections into the knee" components of the conservative-therapy definition quoted above.

6. Absence of contraindications: The record confirms no active infection. [Documentation addressing the remaining contraindication criteria in CPB 0660 — e.g., absence of tibial/femoral shaft deformity, medial/lateral subluxation, flexion contracture greater than 15 degrees, varus/valgus deformity beyond the policy's thresholds, inflammatory or crystalline arthropathy, and large subchondral cysts or extensive focal osteonecrosis — should be confirmed from the surgeon's exam and imaging report and submitted with this appeal, as these specific negative findings were not itemized in the clinical summary provided to me.] Mr./Ms. Carter has a BMI of 29 (below the policy's morbid-obesity threshold of greater than 40) and is a non-smoker. [If Mr./Ms. Carter has diabetes, an HbA1c value less than 8 percent within 3 months prior to surgery should be documented per the policy's Additional Note; the clinical summary provided to me does not indicate a diabetes diagnosis, so I understand this element may not apply, but ask that Dr. Marchetti's office confirm this directly.]

Based on the above, the clinical record — supplemented by the additional chart documentation requested above — meets the medical necessity criteria set out in Aetna Clinical Policy Bulletin 0660 for unicompartmental knee arthroplasty (CPT 27446). I respectfully request that Aetna reverse the denial and approve the requested procedure.

I am submitting this appeal within the 180-day window stated in the denial notice (by 2027-02-15). Please advise if any additional information is needed to complete this review. If this internal appeal is not resolved in Mr./Ms. Carter's favor, I intend to pursue an independent external review through Aetna's External Review Program and/or the Missouri Department of Insurance, as this is a medical-necessity denial under a Missouri-issued commercial/ACA plan.

Please send all correspondence regarding this appeal to the address, phone, and/or email listed above, and reference the Reference Number POC-5BA41AD17E-24277 on all communications.

Thank you for your prompt attention to this matter.

Sincerely,

Rowan Carter
